n: An evening prayer. David asks the God who vindicates him to answer, recalling how God has given him room to breathe in past trouble.

f.g: The God who upholds my cause and declares me in the right.
You gave me space — relief from tight, pressing distress.

n: David asks his opponents how long they will shame his honor, love empty things, and chase lies.

f.g: Emptiness — perhaps idols or worthless plans.

n: They should know the Lord has set apart the faithful for himself and hears their prayers.

f.w: set apart him that is godly for himself
f.g: “Godly” translates ḥasid — one who is loyal and devoted in covenant love.

n: Tremble and don’t sin; reflect quietly on your bed and be still. Good counsel for anyone angry or anxious at night.

f.w: Stand in awe, and sin not
f.g: Or “Be angry, and sin not,” as Paul quotes it.

n: Offer sacrifices with a right heart, and trust in the Lord.
Many ask, “Who will show us anything good?” David answers by praying for the light of God’s face to shine on them — an echo of the priestly blessing.

f.w: lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us

n: God has filled David’s heart with more joy than others feel at a bumper harvest of grain and wine.
David lies down and sleeps in peace, because the Lord alone keeps him safe.

f.w: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep
